most_likely: Malignant neoplasm of left kidney (renal cell carcinoma) treated with radical nephrectomy
summary: Morbidly obese man with CAD s/p CABG, chronic systolic heart failure (EF ~30%), type 2 diabetes and CKD was admitted electively to Urology for an 8 cm left renal mass and underwent laparoscopic left radical nephrectomy with retroperitoneal (para-aortic and hilar) lymph node dissection. Postoperative course was unremarkable apart from anemia (Hgb 8.5–8.9, Hct 26–28), creatinine rising to 2.0–2.3 mg/dL above his prior 1.3–1.6 baseline, and one markedly elevated glucose of 566 mg/dL. He was discharged tolerating diet, ambulating, voiding, on oral analgesia. The principal condition for this stay is the renal malignancy that prompted surgery, with post-nephrectomy renal insufficiency, anemia and diabetic hyperglycemia as secondary/complication codes.
